newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan completes oil products pipeline to Lahore.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan completes oil products pipeline to Lahore.

text.p: Pak-Arab Refinery Co (Parco) has completed a pipeline extension to link the Pakistani cities of Karachi and Lahore, its managing director said on Tuesday

"It's now under testing," Shahid Haq said of the 360-km (225-mile) extension to an existing 864-km (540-mile) products pipeline from the southern port of Karachi to Mahmud Kot, 50 km (31 miles) west of Multan, a city in Punjab province.
"We'll be transporting almost 16,000 tonnes of oil products a day from Karachi -- equivalent to about 1,600 trucks a day -- all underground," Haq told Reuters in an interview.
The pipeline would meet 60 to 70 percent of demand in northern and central Punjab, Pakistan's most populous province, in an "efficient, economic and environment-friendly manner".
Pipeline spurs were also planned from the industrial city of Faisalabad to the towns of Kharian and Sahiwal, Haq added.
Parco, a joint venture of Pakistan and Abu Dhabi, plans to complete a fully integrated $760 million refinery at Mahmud Kot by May 2000 to process 100,000 barrels of crude oil per day.
Pakistan now has a refining capacity of about six million tonnes a year against demand of 12 to 14 million tonnes. "We need at least two refineries by 2000 to 2003," Haq said.
The Parco refinery would be able to supply about 1.3 million tonnes of furnace oil, among other products, to power plants with a combined output of 3,000 megawatts near Mahmud Kot.
"Once the refinery goes into operation, Parco is planning to go into marketing of its own products through its own retail outlets," Haq said.
"Having a cross-country pipeline system and its own refinery, it will be able to offer a very cheap option to consumers by reducing the prices of end-products."

He said Parco was considering building a petrochemical plant at Mahmud Kot to produce paraxylenes, using naphtha produced by the refinery, which could be sold to a purified terephthalic acid (PTA) unit being built by ICI Pakistan Ltd in Karachi.
PTA is an essential intermediate used in the manufacture of polyester fibre, packaging polymers and film.

He said Parco, 60 percent owned by the government of Pakistan and 40 percent by Abu Dhabi, had repaid the original investment of $54 million made in 1981 about 40 times over. It had built assets worth $1 billion without further equity.
